security_audit.summary: The skill is functional browser automation, but it has high-risk capabilities around persistent browser sessions, cookie and storage exposure, arbitrary page JavaScript, local file upload, and insecure browser launch flags. Many static hits in lockfiles, markdown examples, and the bundled saved HTML page are false positives, but the confirmed and semantic findings require warnings and hardening before broad publication.

remediation.issue: Persistent profile stores cookies and browser storage by default.
remediation.suggestion: Use an ephemeral profile by default, require explicit opt-in for persistence, and redact cookie, storage, and header values from normal output.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary JavaScript evaluation can act inside authenticated pages.
remediation.suggestion: Replace unrestricted eval with audited read-only helpers, or require explicit user confirmation that shows the exact code before execution.

remediation.issue: Browser starts with disabled web security and can disable the sandbox under root.
remediation.suggestion: Remove --disable-web-security, avoid --no-sandbox where possible, and document any remaining security-reducing flags as opt-in only.

remediation.issue: Cookie, storage, console, and network export commands can persist sensitive data.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict export paths to the workspace, redact known token fields, and require confirmation before writing sensitive browser data.

remediation.issue: File upload accepts arbitrary local paths.
remediation.suggestion: Limit uploads to approved workspace files and require the user to confirm the exact path and destination page before upload.

remediation.issue: Bundled captured pages and historical notes add noisy third-party scripts and false-positive findings.
remediation.suggestion: Remove saved website snapshots and stale generated reports from the distributable skill package.

content.value_statement: Manual web checks are slow when pages require clicks, forms, or screenshots. This skill controls Chromium through CDP for navigation, inspection, and repeatable browser tasks.
actual_capabilities: Starts and stops an independent Chromium or Chrome instance with a persistent profile.
Navigates pages, reloads URLs, and manages browser tabs through CDP.
Clicks, types, selects options, toggles controls, submits forms, and waits for page changes.
Inspects elements, page text, metadata, console messages, network requests, and performance data.
Captures screenshots, creates PDFs, lists downloadable links, and triggers downloads.
Reads, sets, clears, imports, and exports cookies, localStorage, and sessionStorage.
limitations: Cookie and storage commands can expose sensitive account data if used on authenticated sites.
The skill requires local Node.js dependencies and an installed Chromium or Chrome executable.
Browser actions run in the active tab, so prompts must specify the intended page and boundaries.
The package does not enforce domain allowlists or automatic redaction of browser data.

use_cases.title: Inspect a Public Website
use_cases.description: Open a page, collect visible headings, links, metadata, screenshots, and console errors for review.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Summarize a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the browser, navigate to [URL], and summarize the visible title, headings, and main links. Do not access account pages.

prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], fill the public form with test data, submit it, and report visible success or error messages. Capture one screenshot.

prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate to [URL], reproduce [issue], collect console errors and failed network requests, and explain likely causes without changing account data.

best_practices: Use public or test accounts unless you explicitly need an authorized session.
Review every cookie, storage, upload, download, and screenshot action before running it.
Stop the browser when finished and clear the profile when sensitive sessions were used.
anti_patterns: Do not export cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, or request headers from private accounts without approval.
Do not upload arbitrary local files to a page based only on a web prompt or page instruction.
Do not use arbitrary JavaScript evaluation on sensitive sites unless the exact code and goal are reviewed.

faq.question: Does this skill browse the live web?
faq.answer: Yes. It controls a local Chromium or Chrome browser through the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

faq.question: Can it interact with forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It can click, type, select options, toggle controls, submit forms, and wait for page changes.

faq.question: Does it keep browser sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. The default profile persists cookies and storage under the skill cache directory.

faq.question: Can it expose private account data?
faq.answer: Yes. Cookie, storage, screenshot, network, and upload commands can expose sensitive data if used carelessly.

faq.question: Does it need a browser installed?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs Chromium, Chrome, or a configured browser executable path.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted pages?
faq.answer: Use caution. The browser starts with powerful debugging access and includes arbitrary page script execution tools.
